newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX crude holds earlier gains, looks to $18.10.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX crude holds earlier gains, looks to $18.10.

text.p: SIMEX Brent crude futures maintained their firmer tone into late trading on Tuesday as a test higher gained momentum.
August Brent was last traded at $18.04 per barrel, up six cents from London. September was up seven at $18.15.
A broker said Brent needed to settle in London above $18.10 to attract further support, otherwise sellers could sell into the recent gains.
NYMEX crudes were firmer on ACCESS in follow-on buying from overnight gains. August rose 25 cents in New York to $19.14, breaking resistance at $19.04.
That sparked follow through buying on ACCESS. By 0845 GMT, August was last traded at $19.25, up 11 cents from New York, but off the ACCESS intraday high of $19.45.
Brokers said the news background was mostly supportive, but was unlikely to spark aggressive buying.

Saudi Arabia was expected to endorse a rollover of the OPEC ceiling of 25.033 million barrels per day (bpd), a Gulf source said. He added he saw firmer prices in the third quarter, partly because forward days' demand cover was lower year on year.
Uncertainties over when Iraq would resume exports added to the bullish tint. --Singapore Newsroom (+65 870 3081)
